compatibilityNotes.description: PostgreSQL procedures can control transactions with COMMIT/ROLLBACK, but this procedure doesn't explicitly manage transactions. It will run within the caller's transaction context. SQL Server stored procedures behave similarly unless they contain explicit transaction control.

PostgreSQL uses MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) by default, which differs from SQL Server's locking model. The UPDATE statement will acquire a row-level lock automatically, but concurrent behavior may differ. Consider using SELECT FOR UPDATE if pessimistic locking is required before the update.
PostgreSQL procedures do not return row count messages to clients by default, so SET NOCOUNT ON is unnecessary. This is a behavioral difference that typically requires no action.

No error handling exists in the original procedure. PostgreSQL will raise exceptions on errors (e.g., constraint violations) and rollback the transaction automatically unless caught with an EXCEPTION block.
